name: Evolv Technologies Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Evolv Technologies develops, manufactures, and sells AI-powered security screening systems for high-traffic venues. Its flagship Evolv Express uses advanced sensors and machine learning to detect weapons in unstructured people flows without requiring individuals to stop, remove items, or empty pockets. The company serves 1,200+ customers across education, healthcare, sports, entertainment, and government sectors. Q1 2026 revenue grew 45% YoY to $46.3M with ARR of $127.3M. Founded in 2013, headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Evolv grew Q1 2026 revenue 45% YoY to $46.3M and raised full-year guidance to $175-180M, demonstrating accelerating commercialization of its AI-powered screening platform [1]. The company turned Adjusted EBITDA positive in 2025 ($11.1M) and expanded margins to 8.5% in Q1 2026 [1]. Launched Evolv eXpedite for bag screening, expanding from people-only to comprehensive venue security. However, the company remains a single-product-line security screening business. AI Deployment (2/2): Evolv Express IS an AI product — its entire value proposition is real-time AI weapon detection using advanced sensors and machine learning that has screened billions of people, replacing legacy metal detectors with touchless, AI-driven threat identification across 1,200+ customer sites [2]. Market Share (1/2): Evolv is the clear category leader in AI-powered touchless weapon detection, deployed at NFL stadiums, schools, hospitals, and major venues [2]. However, traditional security vendors including Smiths Detection and Garrett are adding AI capabilities, and the FTC/BBC scrutiny over marketing claims has created reputational headwinds [3]. Pipeline (1/2): Raised 2026 guidance to $175-180M revenue with ARR growing 20% to $127.3M; shift toward ~50% pure subscription model for new deployments strengthens recurring revenue visibility but no specific next-gen products or new verticals named [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Continuous investment in AI detection algorithms trained on billions of scans, with Evolv Insights analytics platform expanding the data offering beyond hardware [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Evolv's mission to 'transform security to create a safer world to live, work, learn, and play' is clear and connects to public safety, but is not deeply distinctive — many security companies express similar goals of making the world safer [2]. The 'privacy by design' approach and vision of making security 'nearly invisible' differentiate somewhat but remain aspirational rather than proven. Community Impact (1/2): Evolv serves schools, houses of worship, and healthcare facilities, directly protecting vulnerable populations; the technology has screened billions of people, representing meaningful social impact in an era of mass shootings [2]. However, no separate philanthropic programs or community investment initiatives with specific dollar amounts identified. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor rating of 3.1/5 based on limited reviews indicates mixed employee sentiment. The board terminated CEO Peter George in October 2024 specifically citing the need 'to improve the company's culture,' directly indicting the trust environment [3]. Three CEO changes in 14 months (George, Ellenbogen interim, Kedzierski) creates organizational instability. Insider Buying (0/2): Co-founder Michael Ellenbogen exercised options and immediately sold 80,745 shares following the Q1 2026 earnings beat [4]. This exercise-and-sell sequence represents net insider selling, not buying conviction. No meaningful open-market insider purchases identified.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on growth-stock metrics with several unavailable. D/E of 34.8% is well below the 70% target, reflecting manageable leverage [5]. ROE of -27.8% scores at floor — the company remains unprofitable on a GAAP basis despite turning Adjusted EBITDA positive [5]. Revenue growth of 45% YoY in Q1 2026 far exceeds the 10% target [1]. Revenue CAGR of approximately 40% over three years ($52.7M in 2022 to $145.9M in 2025) scores at target [1]. Forward P/E of 43.3 scores 0.42, reflecting analyst expectations of approaching profitability [5]. Profit margin of -22.75% scores at floor [5]. PEG ratio unavailable and excluded. Liquidity floor cleared at approximately $17.6M daily dollar volume ($6.25 x 2.82M avg volume). Weighted calculation: (1x1.0 + 2x0.0 + 1x1.0 + 2x1.0 + 1x0.42 + 1x0.0) / 8 x 10 = 5.5 rounded to 6.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Evolv IS an AI company — its entire product line is built on proprietary AI/ML weapon detection algorithms trained on billions of scans across 1,200+ customer sites [2]. AI does not threaten this business; AI IS the business. The physical hardware (advanced sensors, screening portals) combined with proprietary training data creates a moat that pure-software AI cannot replicate — venues cannot deploy a ChatGPT alternative to screen for concealed weapons. The shift toward subscription/SaaS model with Evolv Insights analytics further embeds AI into recurring revenue. However, the risk score is not 8-9 because AI-powered competitors (traditional security vendors adding AI capabilities) could eventually challenge Evolv's technology lead, and the company's relatively small scale (286 employees) limits its defensive moat versus larger incumbents [2]. AI Opportunity (1/1): 100% of Evolv's $46.3M Q1 2026 revenue ($175-180M guided annually) is AI-derived, with Evolv Express and eXpedite being AI-native products and Evolv Insights providing AI-powered analytics as an upsell [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: Evolv shows elements of infinite-game thinking through its mission-driven focus on public safety and long-term subscription model transition, but the forced CEO departure in October 2024 for cultural reasons, three leadership changes in 14 months, SEC investigation into sales practices misconduct, and FTC deceptive marketing probe collectively undermine the organizational foundation needed for sustained infinite play. The company is playing to survive and grow rather than playing to endure.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Protecting people from weapons in schools, hospitals, and public venues connects to a genuine just cause — making public spaces safer in an era of mass violence [2]. The vision of making security 'nearly invisible' while maintaining public safety represents a future state that does not yet exist. However, the mission statement 'transform security to create a safer world' is relatively generic within the security industry, and the company's execution of this cause has been undermined by the SEC investigation into sales misconduct and FTC probe into deceptive marketing claims — practices inconsistent with a deeply held purpose [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The board terminated CEO Peter George in October 2024 specifically citing the need 'to improve the company's culture,' which is a direct indictment of the trust environment [3]. The internal investigation found that 'certain Company personnel engaged in misconduct in connection with' sales practices involving extra-contractual terms hidden from accounting personnel — evidence of a culture where people did not feel safe operating transparently [3]. Glassdoor rating of 3.1/5 with reports of overwork and burnout. Three CEO changes in 14 months (George, Ellenbogen interim, Kedzierski) creates destabilizing organizational uncertainty.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence found of Evolv management acknowledging worthy rivals in a constructive, learning-oriented way. The company positions itself as the category creator and leader in AI-powered screening, but traditional security players like Smiths Detection, Garrett, and CEIA are adding AI capabilities [2]. Evolv's competitive language has focused on differentiation and market creation rather than learning from competitors' strengths. The finite mindset is evident in marketing claims that drew FTC scrutiny [3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The shift from hardware sales to a subscription/SaaS model (targeting 50% pure subscription for new deployments) represents meaningful business model evolution driven by the cause of broader public safety access [1]. The expansion from people screening (Express) to bag screening (eXpedite) and analytics (Insights) shows the company is building platform capabilities rather than remaining a single-product vendor. Non-recurring revenue surged 142% YoY in Q1 2026, indicating product purchase acceleration alongside the subscription transition [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The board's decision to terminate the CEO for cultural reasons rather than tolerating dysfunction shows some courage to prioritize organizational health over operational continuity [3]. The subscription model transition sacrifices near-term revenue recognition for long-term recurring revenue quality. New CEO John Kedzierski (appointed December 2024) brings 23 years of Motorola Solutions experience and represents a deliberate choice of operational discipline over founder-led charisma. However, the company has not demonstrated courage through investing during adversity or walking away from misaligned but profitable revenue.

investment_thesis: Evolv Technologies is the category leader in AI-powered touchless weapon detection, serving 1,200+ customers with technology that has screened billions of people [2]. Q1 2026 revenue surged 45% YoY to $46.3M, beating estimates, and the company raised full-year 2026 guidance to $175-180M with ARR growing 20% to $127.3M [1]. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 8.5% from 6.4% a year ago, and management expects gross margins to reach the mid-50s% for the remainder of 2026 as temporary product mix headwinds subside [1]. TD Cowen named Evolv a top small-cap idea for 2026 with a $10 price target (60% upside from ~$6.25) [4]. The secular tailwind of school safety mandates, venue security requirements, and the replacement cycle from legacy metal detectors provides a multi-year growth runway.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on profitability uncertainty, regulatory risk, and leadership instability. Despite 45% revenue growth, Evolv posted a -22.75% net profit margin and -27.8% ROE — the path to GAAP profitability remains unclear beyond Adjusted EBITDA [5]. The SEC investigation into sales practices found 'misconduct' involving extra-contractual terms hidden from accounting, which led to a financial restatement and eroded investor trust [3]. The FTC separately probed deceptive marketing claims, and the BBC disputed Evolv's claims about UK government testing [3]. The forced CEO termination in October 2024 for cultural reasons, followed by three leadership changes in 14 months, creates execution risk under new CEO John Kedzierski who has been in the role for only seven months [3]. The $1.1B market cap at ~6x forward revenue demands sustained 20%+ growth that could be challenged by traditional security companies (Smiths Detection, Garrett) adding AI capabilities to their established customer relationships. Any high-profile weapon incident at an Evolv-protected venue would be catastrophic for the brand.
key_catalysts: Raised 2026 revenue guidance to $175-180M with 20% ARR growth and improving adjusted EBITDA margins (8.5% in Q1), providing a visible path toward operating leverage and potential GAAP profitability inflection
School safety mandate legislation advancing in multiple U.S. states could accelerate education sector adoption — Evolv's fastest-growing vertical — creating a regulatory tailwind for deployment
TD Cowen top small-cap pick with $10 price target; subscription model transition reaching 50% of new deployments strengthens recurring revenue quality and long-term unit economics
key_risks: SEC investigation and financial restatement — the finding of sales misconduct involving extra-contractual terms hidden from accounting personnel raises material governance concerns and ongoing litigation risk

Leadership instability — three CEO changes in 14 months (George terminated, Ellenbogen interim, Kedzierski appointed December 2024) creates execution risk during a critical growth phase with new CEO only seven months into the role

Detection accuracy and competitive risk — traditional security vendors with established customer relationships are adding AI capabilities, and any high-profile weapon incident at an Evolv-protected venue would severely damage brand credibility
